tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## discord-setup
Discord Server Setup MCP Server

This server provides tools for automating Discord server setup using the Discord Bot API.
It can discover servers, create/manage channels, create/manage roles, configure settings, and apply templates.

Available tool categories:
- Guild: List servers, select active server, get server info
- Channels: Create/edit/delete channels and categories
- Roles: Create/edit/delete/list/reorder roles
- Settings: Configure server verification, content filter, notifications
- Templates: Apply pre-built server templates (gaming, community, business, study-group)

Role hierarchy note: Discord positions are inverted — a HIGHER position number is
higher/more powerful, @everyone is position 0 at the bottom, and newly created
roles default to the bottom. Use list_roles to see the current order, create_role
with placement:"top"/"above"/"below" to rank a role, and reorder_roles with a
top-first orderedRoleIds list rather than hand-computing position numbers.

Prerequisites:
- Discord bot created at https://discord.com/developers/applications
- Bot token configured via DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN environment variable or ~/.discord-mcp/config.json
- Bot invited to Discord server(s) with appropriate permissions (Manage Server, Manage Roles, Manage Channels)

Setup Instructions:
1. Create a Discord application at https://discord.com/developers/applications
2. Add a bot user and copy the bot token
3. Set DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN environment variable or create ~/.discord-mcp/config.json with your token
4. Generate OAuth2 URL with bot scope and required permissions
5. Invite bot to your Discord server(s)

Workflow:
1. Use list_guilds to see available servers
2. Use select_guild to set the active server
3. Use other tools to manage channels, roles, etc.

Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## workos
This server manages the caller's WorkOS workspace: organizations, users, SSO connections, directories, webhooks, branding, feature flags, and more. Call list_operations once to discover operations, then run them with query (reads) or mutate (writes). whoami reports the caller's identity, role, and available environment IDs. An admin may disable mutations or this server entirely for a team; the tool response says so.

This server is a control plane for an existing workspace, not a knowledge base. For WorkOS product, integration, SDK, or tooling questions, don't guess from training data or probe package registries: read https://workos.com/docs. When integrating WorkOS into a codebase, prefer the WorkOS agent skills, which carry the deep integration guides: npx skills add workos/skills

Facts agents often guess wrong: the official WorkOS CLI is the unscoped npm package "workos" (repo github.com/workos/cli). Run npx workos@latest install for the agent-driven AuthKit installer (it edits the codebase), and use its resource commands (--json output) for scripted management. WorkOS SDKs are published under the @workos-inc npm scope (e.g. @workos-inc/node, @workos-inc/authkit-nextjs), but the CLI itself is just "workos".

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

6	
7	**Architecture:** One Node process holds one WorkOS session and one socket to Runlog and fans out to every key face. All decisions live in a pure state machine (`state.ts`) that turns connection state plus the run's offer into what each action draws; the SDK is a thin shell around it. Presses carry the `seq` of the offer they were drawn from, which Plan A's server and page already honor.
8	
9	**Tech Stack:** Node 24, Stream Deck 7.1+, `@elgato/streamdeck` v2 (pinned exact), `@elgato/cli` for scaffold/validate/pack, sdpi-components v4 in the property inspector, Vitest.
10	
11	**Spec:** <https://claude.ai/code/artifact/442de4ff-fd8f-42fd-b511-ba7606b82e1b>
12	
13	**Depends on:** every task of `2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-a.md`. Do not start Task 5 onward until Plan A's Task 11 script drives a real run.
14	
15	## Global Constraints
16	
17	- **Node 24 or later; Stream Deck 7.1 or later** (`Software.MinimumVersion: "7.1"`, `Nodejs.Version: "24"` in the manifest).
18	- **`@elgato/streamdeck` pinned to an exact version** in `streamdeck/package.json`. No `^`.
19	- **No native dependencies in the plugin.** No `sharp`, no `canvas`, no `keytar`. Faces are SVG as `data:image/svg+xml;base64,…` — raw SVG strings are rejected on Stream Deck 7.5 for Windows.
20	- **The refresh token lives in a file of the plugin's own** with owner-only permissions, never in Stream Deck global settings, which the property inspector (a web view) can read. Global settings hold the pinned run and per-action configuration only.
21	- **The socket's life follows configuration, not visibility.** `willAppear` decides what is drawn, never whether the plugin is listening.
22	- **A connected socket holding no run reads *No run open*.** Connecting early must not make keys look live.
23	- **Driving is part of Plus; watching is not.** The plugin never checks entitlement itself — it renders whatever the server's `drove` says.
24	- **The plugin's action UUIDs are `com.scrthq.runlog.<action>`** and never change once shipped; a changed UUID orphans every key a streamer has placed.
25	- **American English throughout.** In-app copy says what a thing does, never why Runlog is good.
26	- **Conventional commit subjects**, lowercase, no period. New scope: `deck`. Existing scopes reused: `api`, `live`, `cli`, `guide`.
27	- **No Claude trailer, session link, or footer** in commits or PR descriptions.
28	- Test commands: `npx vitest run <path>` from the root for every workspace including `streamdeck/`; `npm test -w hosted/infra` for hosted.
29	- `npm run typecheck` must pass before every commit. Task 5 adds `streamdeck/tsconfig.json` to it.
30

32	
33	### Task 1: *Not synced* can be told apart from *No run open*
34	
35	The server does not know about a run that never synced, so an account whose runs are all local would read *No run open* — true and useless. It does know whether the account has **any** owned, unended session. That is enough to say something better.
36	
37	**Files:**
38	
39	- Modify: `hosted/infra/lib/handlers/ws.ts` (`heldRuns`, `tellDecks` from Plan A Task 3)
40	- Test: `hosted/infra/test/ws.test.ts`
41	
42	**Interfaces:**
43	
44	- Consumes: `heldRuns`, `tellDecks` from Plan A.
45	- Produces: the `runs` message gains `any: boolean` — whether the account has any owned, unended, synced run at all.
46	
47	- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**
48	
49	```ts
50	it("says whether the account has any synced run at all", async () => {
51	  const live = memoryLive();
52	  const posted: Array<[string, string]> = [];
53	  const poster: Poster = { post: async (id, data) => (posted.push([id, data]), "ok") };
54	  // manifest for user_a is empty in this deps
55	  const deps = depsWith({ live, poster, sessionsOf: {} });
56	  await route({ requestContext: { routeKey: "$connect", connectionId: "deck1" }, queryStringParameters: { token: "good", as: "deck" } }, deps);
57	  expect(JSON.parse(posted.at(-1)![1])).toEqual({ t: "runs", runs: [], any: false });
58	});
59	```
60	
61	- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**
62	
63	Run: `npm test -w hosted/infra -- ws`
64	Expected: FAIL — `any` is absent.
65	
66	- [ ] **Step 3: Carry it**
67	
68	Change `heldRuns` to return both:
69	
70	```ts
71	const heldRuns = async (sub: string): Promise<{ runs: HeldRun[]; any: boolean }> => {
72	  const { sessions } = await deps.store.manifest(sub);
73	  const mine = sessions
74	    .filter((p) => p.role === "owner" && !p.deletedAt && !p.endedAt)

329	/**
330	 * Where a program keeps its session: the platform's config directory,
331	 * one folder per program, readable by its owner and nobody else. The
332	 * CLI's rule, with the folder name handed in, so the deck and the CLI
333	 * keep separate sessions in the same place.

335	export function configDir(app: string): string {
336	  const base =
337	    process.platform === "win32"
338	      ? (process.env["APPDATA"] ?? join(homedir(), "AppData", "Roaming"))
339	      : process.platform === "darwin"
340	        ? join(homedir(), "Library", "Application Support")
341	        : (process.env["XDG_CONFIG_HOME"] ?? join(homedir(), ".config"));
342	  return join(base, app);
343	}

345	const FILE = "session.json";
346	
347	export function readSession(dir: string): Session | null {
348	  try {
349	    const s = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, FILE), "utf8")) as Partial<Session>;
350	    if (typeof s.accessToken === "string" && typeof s.refreshToken === "string" && typeof s.clientId === "string")
351	      return { clientId: s.clientId, issuer: s.issuer ?? "https://api.workos.com", accessToken: s.accessToken, refreshToken: s.refreshToken, expiresAt: s.expiresAt ?? new Date(0).toISOString() };
352	  } catch {
353	    /* none yet */
354	  }
355	  return null;
356	}
357	
358	export function writeSession(dir: string, session: Session): void {
359	  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
360	  const path = join(dir, FILE);
361	  writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(session), { mode: 0o600 });
362	  try {
363	    chmodSync(path, 0o600);
364	  } catch {
365	    /* Windows: ACLs, not modes; the profile directory is already the user's own */
366	  }
367	}

369	export function forgetSession(dir: string): void {
370	  const path = join(dir, FILE);
371	  if (existsSync(path)) rmSync(path);
372	}

632	/**
633	 * Everything the plugin decides, with nothing from the SDK in it.
634	 *
635	 * A key face is a function of what the plugin knows: whether it is
636	 * signed in, whether its socket is open, which runs are held, which is
637	 * pinned, and what that run last published. `reduce` moves the state on
638	 * one event at a time; the `*Face` functions read it. Keeping them pure
639	 * is what lets the twelve states a key can be in have a test each.
640	 */
641	const FLASH_MS = 3000;
642	
643	export function initial(): DeckState {
644	  return { session: "none", socket: "closed", runs: [], any: false, pinned: null, attached: null, snapshot: null, flash: null };
645	}
646	
647	export function attachedRun(state: DeckState): string | null {
648	  if (state.pinned) return state.runs.some((r) => r.id === state.pinned) ? state.pinned : null;
649	  return state.runs.length === 1 ? state.runs[0]!.id : null;
650	}
651	
652	export function reduce(state: DeckState, event: DeckEvent, now: number): DeckState {
653	  switch (event.t) {
654	    case "session":
655	      return event.state === "ok" ? { ...state, session: "ok" } : { ...initial(), session: event.state, pinned: state.pinned };
656	    case "socket":
657	      return event.state === "open" ? { ...state, socket: "open" } : { ...state, socket: event.state, runs: [], attached: null, snapshot: null };
658	    case "runs": {
659	      const next = { ...state, runs: event.runs, any: event.any };
660	      const attached = attachedRun(next);
661	      // A run that went away takes its numbers with it; a run that is
662	      // still here keeps them until the next snapshot lands.
663	      return { ...next, attached, snapshot: attached === state.attached ? state.snapshot : null };
664	    }
665	    case "pin": {
666	      const next = { ...state, pinned: event.id };
667	      const attached = attachedRun(next);
668	      return { ...next, attached, snapshot: attached === state.attached ? state.snapshot : null };
669	    }
670	    case "snapshot":
671	      return { ...state, snapshot: event.snapshot };
672	    case "drove":
673	      return { ...state, flash: { ref: event.ref, ok: event.ok, ...(event.say ? { say: event.say } : {}), until: now + FLASH_MS } };
674	    case "tick":
675	      return state.flash && state.flash.until <= now ? { ...state, flash: null } : state;
676	  }
677	}

679	/** The state every key shares before any of them has something of its own to say. */
680	function common(state: DeckState): Face | null {

682	  if (state.session === "expired") return { title: "Sign in again", tone: "dim" };
683	  if (state.socket !== "open") return { title: "Offline", tone: "dim" };
684	  if (state.pinned && !state.runs.some((r) => r.id === state.pinned)) return { title: "That run has ended", tone: "dim" };
685	  if (state.runs.length === 0) return state.any ? { title: "No run open", tone: "dim" } : { title: "Not synced", tone: "dim" };
686	  if (!state.attached) return { title: "Pick a run", tone: "dim" };
687	  return null;
688	}

690	function flashed(state: DeckState): Face | null {
691	  if (!state.flash || state.flash.ok) return null;
692	  return { title: state.flash.say ?? "No", tone: "refuse" };
693	}

696	  const c = common(state) ?? flashed(state);

734	function clockText(c: NonNullable<Snapshot["clocks"]>[number], at: string, now: number): string {
735	  const since = c.status === "running" ? now - Date.parse(at) : 0;
736	  const elapsed = c.elapsedMs + since;
737	  const ms = c.seconds === null ? elapsed : Math.max(0, c.seconds * 1000 - elapsed);
738	  const s = Math.floor(ms / 1000);
739	  return `${Math.floor(s / 60)}:${String(s % 60).padStart(2, "0")}`;
740	}

748	  if (field === "unit") return { title: String(snap.unit ?? "—"), tone: "live", when: snap.words?.unit ?? "Unit" };
749	  if (field === "latest") return { title: snap.latest?.text ?? "—", tone: "live" };

752	    return top ? { title: top.name, tone: "live", when: `${top.points} pts` } : { title: "—", tone: "dim", when: "Leader" };

754	  if (field === "clock") {

757	  }

831	import type { Face, Tone } from "./state.ts";
832	
833	/**
834	 * A key face as SVG.
835	 *
836	 * SVG, because it needs no rasterizer and no native module in a package
837	 * the Marketplace installs; base64, because Stream Deck 7.5 on Windows
838	 * rejects a raw SVG string despite the documentation. 144 square is the
839	 * @2x size; the software scales it to any key.
840	 *
841	 * The palette is the app's own: celadon for a live key, kiln for a
842	 * refusal, the muted ink for a key with nothing to do. System sans, since
843	 * a font in an SVG would have to travel as base64 on every redraw.
844	 */
845	const TONE: Record<Tone, { ground: string; ink: string; edge: string }> = {
846	  live: { ground: "#1e2f27", ink: "#e7eae6", edge: "#8cc3a6" },
847	  dim: { ground: "#1b201d", ink: "#8d958f", edge: "#2f3733" },
848	  refuse: { ground: "#33211a", ink: "#e7eae6", edge: "#dd8f63" },
849	};
850	
851	const esc = (s: string) => s.replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">").replace(/"/g, """);
852	
853	/** Up to three lines of about twelve characters; the last one ends in an ellipsis if there was more. */
854	export function wrap(text: string, width = 12, lines = 3): string[] {
855	  const out: string[] = [];
856	  let line = "";
857	  for (const word of text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)) {
858	    if (line && (line + " " + word).length > width) {
859	      out.push(line);
860	      line = word;
861	    } else line = line ? `${line} ${word}` : word;
862	    if (out.length === lines) break;
863	  }
864	  if (out.length < lines && line) out.push(line);
865	  if (out.length > lines || (out.length === lines && (line && !out.includes(line)))) {
866	    out.length = lines;
867	    out[lines - 1] = out[lines - 1]!.slice(0, width - 1) + "…";
868	  }
869	  return out;
870	}
871	
872	export function faceImage(face: Face): string {
873	  const t = TONE[face.tone];
874	  const lines = wrap(face.title);
875	  const size = lines.length === 1 && face.title.length <= 6 ? 34 : 20;
876	  const top = 72 - ((lines.length - 1) * size * 1.15) / 2 + (face.when ? -8 : 0);
877	  const spans = lines.map((l, i) => `<tspan x="72" y="${(top + i * size * 1.15).toFixed(1)}">${esc(l)}</tspan>`).join("");
878	  const when = face.when ? `<text x="72" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="${t.edge}" font-family="ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace">${esc(face.when.slice(0, 18))}</text>` : "";
879	  const svg =
880	    `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 144 144">` +
881	    `<rect width="144" height="144" rx="14" fill="${t.ground}"/>` +
882	    `<rect x="3" y="3" width="138" height="138" rx="12" fill="none" stroke="${t.edge}" stroke-width="3"/>` +
883	    `<text text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="${size}" font-weight="600" fill="${t.ink}" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif">${spans}</text>` +
884	    when +
885	    `</svg>`;
886	  return `data:image/svg+xml;base64,${Buffer.from(svg, "utf8").toString("base64")}`;
887	}

957	import { configDir, deviceFlow, forgetSession, needsRenewal, readSession, refresh, writeSession, type Session } from "@runlog/session";
958	
959	export interface Account {
960	  apiBase: string;
961	}
962	
963	/**
964	 * The deck's session, kept in a file of the plugin's own.
965	 *
966	 * Not in Stream Deck's global settings: those are handed to the property
967	 * inspector, which is a web view, and a refresh token is the one thing
968	 * this plugin holds that must never be. The CLI keeps its session the
969	 * same way, in the same directory tree, under a different name.
970	 */
971	export function sessionDir(): string {
972	  return configDir("runlog-deck");
973	}
974	
975	export function loadSession(): Session | null {
976	  return readSession(sessionDir());
977	}
978	
979	export function signOut(): void {
980	  forgetSession(sessionDir());
981	}
982	
983	async function clientOf(account: Account): Promise<{ clientId: string; issuer: string }> {
984	  const res = await fetch(`${account.apiBase}/api/auth/deck`);
985	  const body = (await res.json()) as { clientId?: string | null; issuer?: string };
986	  if (!body.clientId) throw new Error("this copy of Runlog has no sign-in for a deck");
987	  return { clientId: body.clientId, issuer: body.issuer ?? "https://api.workos.com" };
988	}
989	
990	export async function signIn(account: Account, say: (line: string) => void, open: (url: string) => void): Promise<Session> {
991	  const { clientId, issuer } = await clientOf(account);
992	  const session = await deviceFlow(clientId, issuer, {
993	    fetch: (input, init) => fetch(input, init),

1004	export async function bearer(_account: Account): Promise<string | null> {
1005	  const session = loadSession();
1006	  if (!session) return null;
1007	  if (!needsRenewal(session, Date.now())) return session.accessToken;

1010	    writeSession(sessionDir(), renewed);
1011	    return renewed.accessToken;

diff --git a/.github/workflows/CI-CD.yml b/.github/workflows/CI-CD.yml
index 5f4bc16..7f4a3c4 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/CI-CD.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/CI-CD.yml
@@ -110,6 +110,25 @@ jobs:
 
       - run: npm run build
 
+  # The Stream Deck plugin: its own workspace, built and validated on its
+  # own, since neither the build nor the manifest shape has anything to do
+  # with the app's suite above. Nothing is packed here; the release job
+  # packs the plugin and puts it on the release.
+  Deck:
+    name: Stream Deck plugin
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+      - name: Setup Node and run npm ci
+        uses: ./.github/actions/npm-ci
+        with:
+          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
+
+      - run: npm run build -w streamdeck
+      - run: npx --workspace streamdeck streamdeck validate com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin
+
   InfraTest:
     name: Test the hosting
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
@@ -265,11 +284,12 @@ jobs:
     name: Checks
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     timeout-minutes: 5
-    needs: [Test, InfraTest, Diff]
+    needs: [Test, Deck, InfraTest, Diff]
     if: ${{ always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group') }}
     steps:
       - env:
           TEST: ${{ needs.Test.result }}
+          DECK: ${{ needs.Deck.result }}
           INFRA: ${{ needs.InfraTest.result }}
           DIFF: ${{ needs.Diff.result }}
           EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
@@ -277,9 +297,10 @@ jobs:
           DEPENDABOT: ${{ github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' }}
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
-          echo "Test: $TEST; hosting tests: $INFRA; diffs: $DIFF ($EVENT)"
+          echo "Test: $TEST; deck: $DECK; hosting tests: $INFRA; diffs: $DIFF ($EVENT)"
           ok=true
           [ "$TEST" = "success" ] || { echo "::error::the app's checks did not pass ($TEST)"; ok=false; }
+          [ "$DECK" = "success" ] || { echo "::error::the stream deck plugin's checks did not pass ($DECK)"; ok=false; }
           [ "$INFRA" = "success" ] || { echo "::error::the hosting's checks did not pass ($INFRA)"; ok=false; }
           case "$DIFF" in
             success) ;;
@@ -455,6 +476,25 @@ jobs:
         env:
           OUTPUT: CHANGELOG.md
 
+      # The Stream Deck plugin goes on the release as a file. It is what the
+      # Marketplace submission takes, and what someone installing without the
+      # Marketplace double-clicks. Elgato reads which build a copy came from
+      # out of the manifest and nowhere else, so the release's number goes in
+      # as it is packed: `v0.0.141` becomes `0.0.141.0`, the four-part shape
+      # Elgato wants.
+      - name: Setup Node and run npm ci
+        uses: ./.github/actions/npm-ci
+        with:
+          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
+      - name: Pack the Stream Deck plugin
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          next="${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}"
+          npm run build -w streamdeck
+          npx --workspace streamdeck streamdeck pack com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin \
+            --version "${next#v}.0" \
+            --output dist --force
+
       - name: Tag and publish
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

?? .worktrees/
=== sd gitignore ===
# Node.js
node_modules/

# Stream Deck files
*.sdPlugin/bin
*.sdPlugin/logs
=== release job ===
  # which requires a reviewer, so nothing reaches production or the registry
  # until a person has said so; the dev deploy above needs no such word.
  #
  # Its own lane, with in-progress runs kept: a release being cut finishes,
  # and while one waits for its reviewer the next merge's release takes its
  # place in the queue (GitHub keeps one pending run per lane, the newest),
  # so approving the newest releases everything merged so far, once. What
  # a superseded run would have tagged, the newer one tags; a number already
  # taken is refused rather than reused.
  Release:
    name: Tag and publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: DevDeploy
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: read
    concurrency:
      group: release
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      # Full history, for the tags and the notes since the last one.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # The number the dev build was made with, and no other: a footer on
      # dev that says 0.0.140 is followed by a release called v0.0.140.
      - name: Take the version this build was made with
        id: release
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          next="${{ needs.DevDeploy.outputs.tag }}"
          if [ -z "$next" ]; then echo "::error::the deploy named no version"; exit 1; fi
          # Two builds waiting on a release both name the same next number;
          # once the older one is approved and tagged, the newer counts
          # again from the tag it made, since its commits include the
          # older's. The footer on dev said the old number for a while; the
          # release says the true one, and the summary says it moved.
          if git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/${next}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "${next} is tagged already: a release cut while this one waited took it. Counting again from the latest tag."
            git fetch --tags --quiet origin
            eval "$(bash .github/scripts/next-version.sh auto)"
            echo "moved=${next} -> ${tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            next="$tag"
          fi
          echo "next=${next}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # A GitHub App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN. Anything GITHUB_TOKEN does is
      # barred from starting another run, and that applies to published
      # releases and pushed tags alike. A release created by the App fires
      # the `release: published` event, and production picks it up.
      - name: Mint a token that can trigger the release event
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.CODE_MGR_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.CODE_MGR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      # The notes are the commit titles since the last tag, grouped by type
      # as cliff.toml says; the whole changelog, every release back to the
      # first, goes on the release as a file rather than into the tree, since
      # nothing but this job may write to main.
      - name: Write the release notes
        id: notes
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --unreleased --tag ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }} --strip all
        env:
          OUTPUT: RELEASE_NOTES.md
      - name: Write the whole changelog
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --tag ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}
        env:
          OUTPUT: CHANGELOG.md

      # The Stream Deck plugin goes on the release as a file. It is what the
      # Marketplace submission takes, and what someone installing without the
      # Marketplace double-clicks. Elgato reads which build a copy came from
      # out of the manifest and nowhere else, so the release's number goes in
      # as it is packed: `v0.0.141` becomes `0.0.141.0`, the four-part shape
      # Elgato wants.
      - name: Setup Node and run npm ci
        uses: ./.github/actions/npm-ci
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
      - name: Pack the Stream Deck plugin
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          next="${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}"
          npm run build -w streamdeck
          npx --workspace streamdeck streamdeck pack com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin \
            --version "${next#v}.0" \
            --output dist --force

      - name: Tag and publish
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release create "${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}" \
            --target "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --title "${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}" \
            --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md \
            --latest \
            CHANGELOG.md \
            streamdeck/dist/com.scrthq.runlog.streamDeckPlugin

          {
            echo "### Released ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}"
            echo ""
            if [ -n "${{ steps.release.outputs.moved }}" ]; then echo "The number moved on the way: ${{ steps.release.outputs.moved }}, because a release approved in between took the one dev was built with."; echo ""; fi
            echo "Production deploys from the release event."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

            echo "moved=${next} -> ${tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            next="$tag"
          fi
          echo "next=${next}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # A GitHub App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN. Anything GITHUB_TOKEN does is
      # barred from starting another run, and that applies to published
      # releases and pushed tags alike. A release created by the App fires
      # the `release: published` event, and production picks it up.
      - name: Mint a token that can trigger the release event
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.CODE_MGR_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.CODE_MGR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      # The notes are the commit titles since the last tag, grouped by type
      # as cliff.toml says; the whole changelog, every release back to the
      # first, goes on the release as a file rather than into the tree, since
      # nothing but this job may write to main.
      - name: Write the release notes
        id: notes
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --unreleased --tag ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }} --strip all
        env:
          OUTPUT: RELEASE_NOTES.md
      - name: Write the whole changelog
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --tag ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}
        env:
          OUTPUT: CHANGELOG.md

      # The Stream Deck plugin goes on the release as a file. It is what the
      # Marketplace submission takes, and what someone installing without the
      # Marketplace double-clicks. Elgato reads which build a copy came from
      # out of the manifest and nowhere else, so the release's number goes in
      # as it is packed: `v0.0.141` becomes `0.0.141.0`, the four-part shape
      # Elgato wants.
      - name: Setup Node and run npm ci
        uses: ./.github/actions/npm-ci
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
      - name: Pack the Stream Deck plugin
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          next="${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}"
          npm run build -w streamdeck
          npx --workspace streamdeck streamdeck pack com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin \
            --version "${next#v}.0" \
            --output dist --force

      - name: Tag and publish
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release create "${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}" \
            --target "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --title "${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}" \
            --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md \
            --latest \
            CHANGELOG.md \
            streamdeck/dist/com.scrthq.runlog.streamDeckPlugin

          {
            echo "### Released ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}"
            echo ""
            if [ -n "${{ steps.release.outputs.moved }}" ]; then echo "The number moved on the way: ${{ steps.release.outputs.moved }}, because a release approved in between took the one dev was built with."; echo ""; fi
            echo "Production deploys from the release event."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

=== stream-deck.mdx ===
     1	# A Stream Deck at the table
     2	
     3	Runlog's plugin is in the Stream Deck Marketplace, under **Runlog**. Install it and eight actions appear in the action list: Connect, Run, Do the next thing, Press, Roll, Apply setup, Undo, and Metric. It needs the Stream Deck app at 7.1 or later.
     4	
     5	## Signing in
     6	
     7	Every key's settings carry the same account block: the Runlog address, **Sign in**, **Sign out**, **Reconnect**, and a line saying who is signed in. Leave the address alone unless you run a copy of your own.
     8	
     9	**Sign in** shows a code and a link. Open the link in a browser, type the code, and you are signed in on the deck; the plugin keeps that sign-in in a file of its own, not in the settings the pages read. Signing in is not connecting: press Connect after.
    10	
    11	## Connect
    12	
    13	**Connect** opens the connection, and pressing it again closes it. Nothing is open until you press it, and a connection holding no run closes itself after thirty minutes — the key then says _Idle · press to connect_. A deck that is following a run stays up however long the stream goes.
    14	
    15	Every other key says **Not connected**, with _press Connect_ beneath it, while the connection is off, and **Offline** for the moment it takes to open.
    16	
    17	## The run the deck is on
    18	
    19	The deck presses through the page that holds the run, so it only ever sees a run that is synced to your account and open on a page somewhere: the app in a browser tab, a [dock](#guide/dock), or a browser source. With nothing synced the keys say **Not synced**; with runs synced but none open, **No run open**.
    20	
    21	**Run** names the run the deck is following. Press it to cycle through the runs open to you and pin the next one; its settings list the same runs by name. A pin holds: a pinned run that ends says **That run has ended** rather than moving the deck to whichever run went next. Where one run is open and nothing is pinned, the deck follows that one; where several are open and none is pinned, the keys say **Pick a run**.
    22	
    23	## The keys
    24	
    25	- **Do the next thing** presses whatever the run is waiting on — rolling the table, carrying on, closing the unit, entering the next — and carries the step's own words. Where the step waits on a checklist it ticks everything and presses the step's own button; where it waits on a name, it takes the first suggestion. Tick **Stop at decisions** in its settings and it leaves both to the page.
    26	- **Press** does the one thing you pick in its settings: a move the pack offers, the roll that is waiting, or a preset answer.
    27	- **Roll** throws the dice the run is waiting on. It needs no settings, and is lit only while a roll is on offer.
    28	- **Apply setup** changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool, set in its settings. The list is your library for the pack's tool; a tool has to be attached to the run for the hand-out to reach it.
    29	- **Undo** takes back the last result. It is lit when there is something to take back and dim when there is not.
    30	- **Metric** shows one number and nothing else: the score, the unit, a clock, the last result, the leader, or a counter or resource the pack keeps.
    31	
    32	On a Stream Deck +, Do the next thing and Metric sit on a dial as well as a key. Turning a Metric dial steps through the score, the unit, the clock, the last result and the leader, and a running clock redraws every second.
    33	
    34	A press the run has moved past, or one the page has to take, comes back refused: the key says why for three seconds, then goes back to what it was saying.
    35	
    36	## Keeping the page awake
    37	
    38	Chrome discards tabs it thinks nobody is looking at, and a discarded tab is a run the deck can no longer see. Keep the run in an OBS dock or a browser source, or exempt Runlog from Memory Saver in the browser's settings.
    39	
    40	<Note>
    41	  Where plans are switched on, pressing a run from a deck is part of Plus. Watching one — the run's name and its numbers on your keys — is
    42	  not.
    43	</Note>
=== README ===
     1	# Runlog for Stream Deck
     2	
     3	Runlog is a referee and run log for dice-driven games: it draws the tables, keeps the score and the clocks, and remembers what happened. This plugin puts a run on the deck's keys — the press the run is waiting on, a move, undo, and a number from the run on each key.
     4	
     5	## The keys
     6	
     7	- **Connect** — opens the connection to your Runlog account, and closes it again.
     8	- **Run** — names the run the deck is on; press to cycle through the runs you have open, or pick one in its settings.
     9	- **Do the next thing** — presses whatever the run is waiting on, in the step's own words.
    10	- **Press** — one move, the roll that is waiting, or a preset answer, set in the key's settings.
    11	- **Roll** — throws the dice the run is waiting on.
    12	- **Apply setup** — changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool.
    13	- **Undo** — takes back the last result.
    14	- **Metric** — one number from the run: the score, the unit, a clock, the last result, the leader, or a counter or resource the pack keeps.
    15	
    16	Do the next thing and Metric also sit on a dial on a Stream Deck +.
    17	
    18	## What it needs
    19	
    20	- The Stream Deck app, 7.1 or later, on macOS 12 or Windows 10 and up.
    21	- A Runlog account, signed in from any key's settings.
    22	- A run synced to that account and open in a browser, a dock or a browser source: the deck presses through the page holding the run.
    23	- Where plans are switched on, Plus to press a run from the deck. Watching one costs nothing.
    24	
    25	## Where to read more
    26	
    27	The guide's [A Stream Deck at the table](https://runlog.scrthq.com/guide/stream-deck) sets the keys up, page by page. [Runlog](https://runlog.scrthq.com) is the app.

3	/**
4	 * A key face as SVG.
5	 *
6	 * SVG, because it needs no rasterizer and no native module in a package
7	 * the Marketplace installs; base64, because Stream Deck 7.5 on Windows
8	 * rejects a raw SVG string despite the documentation. 144 square is the
9	 * @2x size; the software scales it to any key.

11	 * The palette is the app's own: celadon for a live key, kiln for a
12	 * refusal, the muted ink for a key with nothing to do. System sans, since
13	 * a font in an SVG would have to travel as base64 on every redraw.
14	 */
15	const TONE: Record<Tone, { ground: string; ink: string; edge: string }> = {
16	  live: { ground: "#1e2f27", ink: "#e7eae6", edge: "#8cc3a6" },
17	  dim: { ground: "#1b201d", ink: "#8d958f", edge: "#2f3733" },
18	  refuse: { ground: "#33211a", ink: "#e7eae6", edge: "#dd8f63" },

21	const esc = (s: string) => s.replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">").replace(/"/g, """);

23	/**
24	 * Glyph widths in em for the system sans at weight 600 - Segoe UI Semibold
25	 * on Windows, and near enough everywhere else. Counting characters was
26	 * pessimistic: "connected" is nine narrow letters and fits at 26, but a
27	 * count of ten sends it to 22. So the face measures instead, in classes
28	 * coarse enough to read and close enough that the rendered ink stays
29	 * inside the frame.
30	 */
31	const EM: Record<string, number> = {};
32	for (const c of "ijl'.,:;!| ") EM[c] = 0.28;
33	for (const c of "ftrI") EM[c] = 0.36;
34	for (const c of "mw") EM[c] = 0.85;
35	for (const c of "MW") EM[c] = 0.92;
36	EM["…"] = 0.9;

38	function em(ch: string): number {
39	  const known = EM[ch];
40	  if (known !== undefined) return known;
41	  if (/[0-9a-z]/.test(ch)) return 0.55;
42	  if (/[A-Z]/.test(ch)) return 0.68;
43	  return 0.6;
44	}
45	
46	/** How wide a line of text draws, in px, at this font size. */
47	export function measure(text: string, size: number): number {
48	  let w = 0;
49	  for (const ch of text) w += em(ch);
50	  return w * size;
51	}
52	
53	/**
54	 * The frame's usable width. 144 less 8 either side: the stroke is 3px wide
55	 * centered at x=3, so 8 leaves 5px of clear ground inside it. Text is
56	 * centered on 72, so a line no wider than this never reaches x=8 or x=136.
57	 */
58	const LINE = 144 - 2 * 8;
59	const MAX_LINES = 3;
60	
61	/**
62	 * The `when` line's own type: 18px monospace, a flat 0.6em per glyph rather
63	 * than the title's per-glyph measurement. 128px at 18px holds 11 characters
64	 * (128 / (18 * 0.6) = 11.85); a twelfth never fits.
65	 */
66	const WHEN_SIZE = 18;
67	const WHEN_MAX = 11;
68	
69	/**
70	 * Fit `when` to `WHEN_MAX` characters. A word boundary that still leaves at
71	 * least six characters reads better than a stub, so that is tried first;
72	 * otherwise the cut falls back to characters. Either way an "…" marks what
73	 * was cut, and nothing kept ever runs past `WHEN_MAX`.

75	function ellipsizeWhen(text: string): string {
76	  if (text.length <= WHEN_MAX) return text;
77	  let cut = "";
78	  for (const word of text.split(" ")) {
79	    const next = cut ? `${cut} ${word}` : word;
80	    if (next.length > WHEN_MAX) break;
81	    cut = next;
82	  }
83	  if (cut.length < 6) cut = text.slice(0, WHEN_MAX);
84	  return `${cut}…`;

87	/**
88	 * Greedy word wrap by measured width: pack words onto a line up to `width`
89	 * px at `size`, at most `lines` lines. A word too wide for a line of its
90	 * own is broken by characters and carries on below. The last line gets an
91	 * ellipsis if any text was left over.
92	 */
93	export function wrap(text: string, size: number, width = LINE, lines = MAX_LINES): string[] {
94	  const words = text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
95	  const out: string[] = [];
96	  let i = 0;
97	  while (i < words.length && out.length < lines) {
98	    const word = words[i]!;
99	    if (measure(word, size) > width) {
100	      let cut = "";
101	      for (const ch of word) {
102	        if (measure(cut + ch, size) > width) break;
103	        cut += ch;
104	      }
105	      // One glyph always goes, or a face narrower than its own type would
106	      // loop here forever.
107	      if (cut === "") cut = [...word][0]!;
108	      out.push(cut);
109	      words[i] = word.slice(cut.length);
110	      continue;
111	    }
112	    let line = word;
113	    i++;
114	    while (i < words.length && measure(line + " " + words[i], size) <= width) {
115	      line += " " + words[i];
116	      i++;
117	    }
118	    out.push(line);
119	  }
120	  if (i < words.length && out.length > 0) {
121	    let last = out[out.length - 1]!;
122	    while (last.length > 0 && measure(last + "…", size) > width) last = last.slice(0, -1);
123	    out[out.length - 1] = last + "…";
124	  }
125	  return out;
126	}
127	
128	/**
129	 * The type scale, biggest first. Every step gets the same three lines and
130	 * the same 128px; what changes is how much of a phrase that holds. A title
131	 * takes the first step that keeps every word whole; one too long for the
132	 * last step is wrapped to it anyway and ellipsized rather than drawn over
133	 * the frame.
134	 */
135	const SCALE = [40, 34, 30, 26, 22] as const;
136	
137	/** Whether wrapping at this size keeps every word of the phrase. */
138	function whole(text: string, size: number): boolean {
139	  return wrap(text, size).join(" ") === text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).join(" ");
140	}
141	
142	function typeset(text: string): { lines: string[]; size: number } {
143	  const size = SCALE.find((s) => whole(text, s)) ?? SCALE[SCALE.length - 1]!;
144	  return { lines: wrap(text, size), size };

169	    `<title>${esc(face.title)}</title>` +
170	    `<rect width="144" height="144" rx="14" fill="${t.ground}"/>` +
171	    `<rect x="3" y="3" width="138" height="138" rx="12" fill="none" stroke="${t.edge}" stroke-width="3"/>` +

174	    `</svg>`;

I have everything I need. Here is the review.

---

## Summary

`the-deck-arrives` adds a well-built Stream Deck plugin: 29 commits, ~5,300 added lines, eight actions, and a clean separation between a pure reducer (`state.ts`) and a thin SDK shell. All six verification commands pass — 105 tests across 12 files, typecheck, `lint:docs` (0 issues/93 files), `format:check`, `npm run build -w streamdeck`, and `streamdeck validate` reports **Validation successful**. The architecture is the best part of this branch: every key face is a pure function of one state object, and `state.test.ts` has a case per face. The socket's generation counter, with tests for a superseded dial, a retired close, and a late snapshot, catches a class of reconnect bug that normally ships.

Two things stop it. First, `bearer()` has no single-flight guard around a **rotating** refresh token, so two overlapping calls — routine during play — produce a spurious "Sign in again" mid-run. Second, **the branch is four commits behind `origin/main`, and those four commits (#291–#294) are the page half this plugin presses against**: `offer.setups` and `takePress`'s `setup` branch exist only on main. The merge is clean (`git merge-tree` produces a tree with no conflicts), but nothing here has been built or tested against what will actually ship. Note also that the review diff `e4c50ac..b6e8b06` is misleading — `e4c50ac` is not an ancestor of HEAD (merge-base is `ecb2fc2`), so the ~718 deletions it shows in `apps/web/src/run/` are main's work, not reverts on this branch. I reviewed against `ecb2fc2..b6e8b06`.

## Findings

### Critical

**1. Concurrent renewal burns the rotating refresh token — `streamdeck/src/session.ts:70-84`**

`bearer()` reads the session off disk, and if `needsRenewal` is true calls `renew()` with no guard. Two callers can be in flight at once: `openWire.open()` (`socket.ts:86`) and `fetchSnapshot()` (`socket.ts:59`), and `fetchSnapshot` fires on every `changed` ring. Two rings in the same turn — a roll that publishes twice — both read the same `refreshToken` and both POST it. WorkOS rotates on every renewal, so the second is refused. In `fetchSnapshot` that silently drops a snapshot (recoverable). In `open()` the refusal returns `null`, which dispatches `{ t: "session", state: "expired" }` (`socket.ts:93`) and `reduce` resets to `initial()` — the whole deck goes to **Sign in again** while the session is in fact fine. Where the issuer treats refresh-token reuse as a compromise signal, it becomes a real sign-out mid-stream.

The 60-second `RENEW_MARGIN_MS` against a 1-hour token means this window opens once an hour of active play. Smallest fix — share the in-flight promise:

```ts
let renewing: Promise<string | null> | null = null;
export async function bearer(_account: Account): Promise<string | null> {
  const session = loadSession();
  if (!session) return null;
  if (!needsRenewal(session, Date.now())) return session.accessToken;
  renewing ??= renew(session)
    .then((r) => (writeSession(dir(), r), r.accessToken))
    .catch(() => null)
    .finally(() => { renewing = null; });
  return renewing;
}
```

`session.test.ts:49` already proves rotation is written back; add a case that fires two `bearer()` calls and asserts `fetch` was called once.

**2. The branch does not carry the page half it presses — needs `origin/main` merged in**

`streamdeck/src/actions/setup.ts:22` sends `{ press: "answer", answer: { setup: id } }`, and `state.ts:26` declares `setups` on the mirrored `Offer`. On this branch, `apps/web/src/run/offer.ts` has no `setups` field and `takePress.ts` has no `setup` branch — an Apply setup press would fall through to the `declareSubject` check and come back *"The run is not asking for that."* On `e4c50ac` both exist (`offer.ts:26`, `takePress.ts:89-94`). Merge `origin/main` before opening so CI runs against the real pair. The merge itself is clean.

### Important

**3. `redrawAll` swallows nothing and catches nothing — `streamdeck/src/actions/base.ts:100-102`**

```ts
for (const a of this.actions) void a.getSettings<S>().then((s) => this.draw(a, s));
```

No `.catch`. `draw()` guards only the key branch (`base.ts:81-88`); `this.face(...)` at line 73 and `await action.setFeedback(feedback)` at line 96 are both unguarded, and `face()` reads a snapshot cast `as never` straight off the wire (`socket.ts:65`) with no validation. The SDK installs `process.once("uncaughtException")` (`dist/plugin/logging/index.js:27`) — `once`, so the first rejection is logged and the second takes the plugin down. Add `.catch((e) => streamDeck.logger.error(...))` on line 101 and move the dial branch inside the existing try.

**4. Every inspector depends on a third-party CDN at load — all eight `ui/*.html`, e.g. `press.html:6`**

`<script src="https://sdpi-components.dev/releases/v4/sdpi-components.js">`, with no `integrity` and no version beyond `v4`. Offline, or if that host is down, `const { streamDeckClient } = SDPIComponents;` throws before anything renders — the account block, the run picker, the field picker and the setup picker are all dead, so the streamer cannot even sign in. For a Marketplace plugin, vendor the file into `ui/` (it is one JS file, no build) or at minimum pin an exact release with `integrity` + `crossorigin`.

**5. `base.ts` and `plugin.ts` have no tests, and both hold logic that fails silently**

- `send()` (`base.ts:113-141`) is the only thing between a press and the streamer knowing what happened: `showOk` on a verdict, `showAlert` on a refusal, the `VERDICT_MS` fallback alert, and the cancel-on-deck-off. None of it is exercised — the action tests mock `../plugin.ts` so the subscription never receives a flash.
- `codeFromLines()` (`plugin.ts:132-140`) parses `packages/session/src/flow.ts:104-105`'s exact output with `/^ {2}Open {2}(\S+)$/` and `/^ {2}Code {2}(\S.*)$/`. It matches today, but `flow.ts` is shared with the CLI; reword either line and the sign-in code never reaches the inspector, with nothing to catch it. Export it and assert it against real `deviceFlow` `say` output.
- `connect.ts` and `undo.ts` have no press test, unlike the other six actions.

### Minor

6. `streamdeck/package.json:1` has no `"name"` and no `"private": true`, unlike every other workspace.
7. Every build prints `TS5096: allowImportingTsExtensions can only be used when noEmit or emitDeclarationOnly is set`. Noise that trains people to ignore the build's warnings.
8. `streamdeck/src/face.ts:1` imports `from "./state"` with no `.ts`; the other eleven modules all use `./state.ts`.
9. `rollup.config.mjs:38` — `include: ["src/**/*.ts", "../packages/**/src/**/*.ts"]` type-checks every package in the repo during the deck build. Only `packages/session` is imported; narrow it.
10. `CI-CD.yml:509` hard-codes `streamdeck/dist/com.scrthq.runlog.streamDeckPlugin`. I traced `@elgato/cli` 1.9.0 (`bin/streamdeck.mjs`, `cd()` strips `.sdPlugin`) and the name is right — but the Deck job never packs, so the first proof is a release that either works or fails at `gh release create`. Use `streamdeck/dist/*.streamDeckPlugin`, or add a pack step to the Deck job.
11. `base.ts:52` and `:76-78` log the face title and `JSON.stringify(settings)` at `info` — the pack's own words (move labels, run names, pack titles, a declared subject) go into the plugin log. No token is logged, which is the part that matters, but worth knowing before sending logs to Elgato support.
12. `base.ts:57` unsubscribes on `this.actions.length === 0`. `actions` is the *visible* set; if the disappearing action is still counted there, the subscription is never released. Harmless, but the intent deserves an assertion.
13. `press.html:62` saves the typed answer on `change`, so a value typed and left without blurring is lost.
14. `packages/session/src/store.ts:12` drops the `darwin` branch the plan specified (`~/Library/Application Support`). I checked `e4c50ac:packages/cli/src/account.ts:58` — the CLI had no darwin branch either, so this is a faithful move and no macOS session is stranded. Flagging only because it departs from the written plan.
15. `writeSession` (`store.ts:39-48`) is a non-atomic `writeFileSync`; a crash mid-write leaves an unreadable session and a forced re-sign-in. Temp-then-rename removes it.
16. `pin()` (`run.ts:47`) read-modify-writes global settings, which can clobber an `apiBase` the inspector is writing at the same moment.

## What is good

- **`state.ts`.** Every face is a pure function of one reducer's state, with a test per case. This is what makes the whole branch reviewable, and the `?? []` guard in `setupFace` for an older page's offer is exactly the right instinct.
- **The generation counter in `socket.ts`**, with tests named for a superseded dial's refusal, a retired socket's close, and a snapshot that arrives after its connection is gone.
- **Token handling.** The session is a 0600 file, never in global settings (which the inspector web view reads), and the rotated refresh token is written back — with a test whose name says why.
- **No redraw storms.** `tick` returns the identical object when nothing is moving, so an idle deck redraws zero times and a running clock exactly once a second.
- **Cross-boundary shapes all check out** against `e4c50ac:hosted/infra/lib/handlers/ws.ts`: `hello` is what makes the server send the runs list (`ws.ts:284`), `from` is added server-side (`ws.ts:545`, so the plugin is right to omit it), and the `drove` verdict's optional `seq` is honored on both ends.
- **No pack text reaches `innerHTML`** — the inspectors build options with `createElement` + `textContent` throughout.
- **Docs.** Plain, American English, no marketing; I checked each claim in `stream-deck.mdx` against the code (eight actions, the dial pair, the thirty-minute idle-off, the three-second refusal, *Not synced* vs *No run open*) and every one holds. The `/guide/stream-deck` path form matches the convention in `docs/README.md`.
- **Private-pack boundary is clean.** The only pack vocabulary in the diff is the demo pack the plan itself uses (The Long Kiln, Roll the Weather, bowls) plus `kiln` as a design-system color name.

One housekeeping note: while I was reviewing, `streamdeck/src/face.ts` and `face.test.ts` changed in the working tree (the `when` line grown to 18px with a new `ellipsizeWhen`). That work is not in `b6e8b06`; I re-ran the face tests against it (20 pass) but reviewed the commit.

## Verdict

**Needs fixes first.** Finding 1 is four lines and prevents a spurious sign-out mid-stream; finding 2 is a merge. Findings 3–5 are worth doing in the same pass. Everything else can follow.
